text_blocks.snippet: To prevent ice dams on a Utah roof, keep the roof cold and the water flowing. Stop warm air from escaping your house into the attic, and make sure meltwater has a clear path off the roof. Combine good insulation, proper airflow, and clear gutters to stop ice from building up during heavy mountain snow and freeze-thaw cycles.
snippet_highlighted_words: keep the roof cold and the water flowing

list.snippet: Seal air leaks around attic hatches, light fixtures, and plumbing pipes.

Add attic insulation
to reach Utah building code standards (R-49 or higher) so heat stays in your living space.
Install rafter vents (baffles) to keep insulation from blocking air moving up from your soffits.
Clear soffit vents at the low edge of your roof so fresh, cold outside air enters the attic.

Clear ridge vents
at the top of your roof so warm air escapes instead of warming the roof deck.
Clean gutters and downspouts late every fall so melting snow has a clear path to drain away from your foundation.

Pull heavy snow off
lower roof edges with a long-handled roof rake after big storms.
Install heat cables (like a DIY roof de-icing kit) along problem eaves and gutters to create active drainage paths.

Use ice-and-water shield
(waterproof membrane) under your shingles along the eaves whenever you replace your roof.

references.title: Easy Heat Roof Gutter Cable ADKS
references.snippet: Keep your gutters and downspouts flowing all winter long! Prevent ice dam formation and the costly damage it can cause by installing the EasyHeat ADKS kit. Ice dams are frozen ridges of melting snow that stop the water from flowing off the roof. Ice dams can form on roofs, eaves, dormers, roof valleys, gutters, skylights and downspouts and can cause shingle damage, water leakage into the roof, damage to insulation, moisture leakage into walls and ceilings, and gutter or downspout problems. The ADKS de-icing cable is installed over the unheated portions of the roof above the overhang or into gutters or downspouts to create an ice-free pathway for melting water to drain. The ADKS cable plugs into a standard 120 VAC GFCI protected three-wire grounded outlet. Prevents dangerous icicles from building up over pathways and doors. Keeps gutters and down spouts open and clear for water to flow. The use of a temperature and moisture sensing control such as EasyHeat's RS-2 is highly recommended. It measures both temperature and moisture to turn the system on or off in response to changing weather conditions.
